pageCache.pageTitle: Independent Private School in Hampshire - Meoncross School
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Meoncross School
A child's educational journey should be as unique as they are. We pride ourselves on our holistic approach whereby every child has the individual attention they need to thrive and succeed both in and out of the classroom. At Meoncross, every child is safe to say ‘I can be the best possible ME’. We are very proud to be a through school for children aged 2.5 - 16 years, meaning we can welcome children into our school at any point in their educational journey. This could be at a natural key stage transition point such as starting 'big school' in Reception, Juniors in Year 3, or Upper School in Year 7, or anything in between. Academic achievement is high, but so is our focus on wellbeing, as we know that happy children are high achieving children. We nurture our pupils and develop the characteristics and qualities we know they will need to build bright futures.
Excellent Academics
We were ranked 10th nationally in Times Parent Power Guide in 2026, and we have a proven track record of achieving excellence when it comes to academic results. Our pupils routinely achieve results well above the national average, from our Early Years to key Primary stages and GCSE results.
Holistic Approach
Emotional intelligence is just as important as academic achievement and we want our pupils to be confident, compassionate and capable young people. We believe it’s crucial to develop a child’s character through teaching transferable skills that will help them to thrive in the future.
We Are Meoncross
We have a strong family ethos, and instil a sense of great pride in our school community. We look after, support and encourage each other to always be our best.
At Meoncross, we often talk about the right school being “a feeling”, and in our school film we wanted to convey what a special and unique feeling there is at our school.
We hope you enjoy watching our film, and we look forward to welcoming you to experience Meoncross in person if you would like to find out more.
“Family is our central value and that means we are accepting, that we are kind to each other, we seek to understand and appreciate each other.”
- Sarah Ebery, Head of Meoncross
The Times Parent Power Schools Guide 2026
Meoncross School was ranked 10th in The Times Parent Power Schools Guide for 2026. We are incredibly proud of this achievement and to have had the exceptional work of our pupils and staff recognised in such a prestigious publication. We have placed 10th in the ‘Top independent secondary schools with no sixth forms’ category. The Guide is compiled based on examination results.
Our Nursery provides an exceptional start for children from 2 years old
Specialist teaching in Ballet, Music, French, P.E, Drama, plus Happy Diggers, Mini Masterchefs, Beach School, and Outdoor Learning.
Top 20 Nursery in the South East by daynurseries.co.uk
Makaton Friendly Status
Millie’s Mark for Excellence in First Aid
15 hours Early Years funding available

~ Community and Belonging ~Being part of a community that cares is at the heart of Meoncross School. Knowing each child as an individual, supporting their strengths and working together to give everyone roots to grow and wings to fly.
Summer may be in session, but our Admissions Team is still here for you! ☀️If you`re exploring school options and would like to learn more about life at our school, we`re just a phone call or email away.From admissions enquiries to arranging a visit, we`re happy to help every step of the way.📞 Contact us today to start the conversation. 01329 662182.
The move to Year 7 is one of the biggest moments in a child`s education.For some children, it feels exciting.For others, it can feel overwhelming.At Meoncross School, every child is known, supported and encouraged from day one.Small classes and strong pastoral care help pupils settle quickly, build confidence and thrive.Discover how we make the transition to secondary school feel positive and exciting.Applications for September 2027 are now open, with limited spaces for this September.
The sun finally emerged as we staged our long-awaited production of Much Ado About Nothing. With a cast ranging from Year 7 to Year 10, we braved the changeable weather to rehearse and perform outdoors, framing this charming story of love and deception against the leafy backdrop of the school grounds. The pupil actors did a splendid job, handling Shakespeare`s language with aplomb. We even got treated to a Globe style jig at the end! Bravo to all.

Meet our Head
I hope it will be clear to you how important our values are to us as a community; we genuinely strive to live by them seeing ourselves as a family where optimism and kindness stand shoulder to shoulder with opportunities and high academic achievement. Just like any family, we know that every child has their strengths and their struggles, and we encourage and support them all, whilst genuinely appreciating and understanding the individuals they are. Only by getting this mix right, can we hope to ensure that all our pupils leave Meoncross ready to flourish in this constantly evolving world of ours. Sarah Ebery Head of Meoncross
Join us for an Open Morning
At our Open Mornings you will have the opportunity to meet our Head and other key members of staff, and learn more about what a Meoncross education looks like. Please click below to register to attend our upcoming Open Morning. We can’t wait to meet you! Upcoming Open Events: Open Evening - Thursday 1sdt October 2026, 6-8pm Open Morning - Tuesday 6th October 2026, 10am-12pm
FACILITIES & LOCATION
An excellent location to learn
Our pupils learn and discover in a range of facilities, located a mile from the Solent on the rural edge of Stubbington. Meoncross pupils benefit from excellent learning environments both on and off-site. Our classrooms are bright, vibrant, inspirational learning spaces where pupils can access various creative and academic subject specialist equipment and resources.
A free parent & child group
Join us every Wednesday, 10.30am-11.20am, (during term time) for our Parent and Child Group – perfect for children aged 0–4. Our dedicated and friendly team go above and beyond to create a warm, welcoming environment where little ones can explore, play, and learn through sensory activities, crafts, and plenty of fun. New theme each week announced on our social media.
An education as unique as your child

Take a look at our wonderful school
We have a variety of ways to experience our school from private tours, to school in action open mornings and taster days. All of which allow you and your child to experience life at Meoncross first hand. However you choose to visit and experience our school, we promise a warm welcome. Our upcoming Open Mornings
Here at Meoncross, we are in the lucky position to be able to welcome new pupils all year round. Our experienced staff are highly skilled at settling children into our wonderful setting at any time within the academic year. We warmly invite you to come and look around and meet our friendly Admissions team. Places are limited, so early booking is advised.

Take a guided tour of our school, led by our pupils who can share what the school has to offer for your child.
An opportunity to speak about our admissions process with our team who will answer any questions you may have.
Visit and explore our classrooms where you can speak with our fantastic teachers to see first-hand, how they bring learning to life.
Open Mornings
We hold regular School in Action Open Mornings throughout the academic year, which are a fantastic opportunity to see our pupils happy and engaged in their lessons, meet our inspirational teachers and see how your child would be given the opportunity to fully flourish at Meoncross. Every year, in September, we hold an Open Week for families to come along and see just what makes Meoncross the first choice school for so many families.
Mid-Year Admissions Open Morning
Last academic year, more than half of all our new pupils joined us mid-year. This can be due to several reasons; families relocating, pupils who are more able and need to be academically stretched, or possibly even gaps in learning caused by the impact of the pandemic. Whatever the reason for a mid-year start, we are here to help as much as we can, and we are very used to and experienced with welcoming children mid-year.
Enjoy a private tour tailored to you
In addition to our SIA Open Mornings and Open Week, we are delighted to offer private tours of our school throughout the term, by appointment only. During the visit, you will be toured by our Admissions Manager, and also have the opportunity to meet our Senior Leadership Team (SLT) to discuss any details regarding your child. If you cannot visit us in person for whatever reason, our Senior Leadership Team are happy to offer an online virtual meeting at a mutually convenient time as an introduction to our school. Please feel free to get in touch to learn more about our welcoming environment, small classes and high-quality teaching tailored to your child’s individual needs.

pageCache.text:
Vision & Values
Ensuring the best educational experience for your child
At Meoncross, we all work together to give everyone roots to grow and wings to fly. In reality, this means creating and maintaining an environment where everyone can grow to be themselves and leave us ready for a full life.
Our school ethos
Our core values
Integrity We always do the right thing, even when it is difficult.
Family We look after each other, work as a team and enjoy being part of a caring community.
Resilience We believe in ourselves and see setbacks as opportunities to try and try again.
Optimism We are happy, confident and enthusiastic learners.
Achievement We thrive on challenge and always aim to succeed.
Kindness We are generous in thought, word and action.
Adventure We are curious and excited about our learning, prepared to take risks and try new things.
Meoncross School

Inspection Reports
ISI Regulatory Compliance and Educational Quality Inspection Report
September 2024
An inspection is a thorough process carried out by the Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI) and overseen by the Department for Education (DfE), typically occurring every three years. In September 2024, Meoncross School experienced a comprehensive inspection by the ISI using the newly implemented Framework 23, which was introduced in September 2023. Importantly, this new framework no longer provides overall judgments or grades from the ISI. Instead, the inspection report is organised around five key areas, where inspectors carefully outline commendations for 'Standards Met' and offer insightful feedback, addressing areas needing improvement where standards are not yet fulfilled. We are thrilled that Meoncross achieved the best possible rating of 'Standards Met' in all five areas. This accomplishment reflects the hard work and commitment of our exceptional team.
The school successfully meets its aim of providing a supportive family-like environment where pupils can thrive both personally and academically.
The provision and quality of education, training and recreation supports the development of confident, capable, and well-rounded pupils.
Academic outcomes for pupils are good for pupils throughout the school, with pupils making progress over time and achieving well at GCSE.
There is an extensive extra-curricular provision with clubs including cooking, music and sports, which are accessible to all ages.
Pupils demonstrate respectful relationships with adults and each other.
Meoncross School

Extra Curricular Activities
An exciting extra-curricular provision
At Meoncross, we are firm believers that learning happens beyond the classroom, and we offer varied and valuable opportunities for our pupils to enjoy. We run a range of fun, exciting and interesting extra-curricular activities both at lunchtimes and after school every week for all children in Reception to Year 11.

An activity for everyone
We run a range of fun, exciting and engaging extra-curricular activities at lunchtime and after school every week. Clubs and societies run throughout the year, offering our pupils many opportunities to broaden their horizons by trying new things, discovering hidden talents and becoming intellectually and culturally curious beyond the curriculum. Extra-curricular activities also offer pupils the chance to socialise with their peers while participating in an enjoyable event. A number of our extra-curricular activities are sports based and seasonal; namely professional tennis coaching, football, netball shooting, hockey, cricket and rounders.
Drama is also well represented, with a weekly drama club, and annual productions which include both a Shakespeare play in the autumn, and a Musical in the summer. Clubs are offered in other areas, and the following is a non-exhaustive list: Newspaper Club, Debating, Film Appreciation Society, First Aid Club, Gardening, Table-top Games, Scrap-booking, Speed-stacking, Computer Coding, Chess, Cookery, Gig-rowing and a twice termly Culture Club lecture. In addition, out-of-hours weekly academic workshops are offered to pupils in a variety of subjects, either in preparation for examinations or as the need arises.
Wider Opportunities
At Meoncross, we are firm believers that learning happens beyond the classroom, and we offer varied and valuable opportunities for our pupils to enjoy.
A range of fun, exciting and interesting extra-curricular activities both at lunchtimes and after school every week for all children in Reception to Year 11.
We offer regular focused days throughout the year where pupils across the school engage deeper learning, within and outside the curriculum.
Working closely with our School Values, we offer our pupils opportunities that compliment and enrich their learning. By offering this, our pupils:

They develop even greater maturity and balanced view of society and cultures and appreciate how they can play such an important part in making a positive difference to other people and our planet.

Educational Technology
Prepared for the future
Technology has become a fundamental part of our education, not only allowing us to deliver great teaching and learning but as a platform for collaboration and productivity. We have witnessed first-hand the positive impact it can have, putting pupils at the heart of their learning by increasing engagement, developing intrinsic interpersonal skills and preparing them for the future of adult life.
We are an innovative school when it comes to the use of technology and as well as our 1:1 device programme, we also use the most advanced software technologies to support learning. We use many systems, such as our Firefly VLE, OneNote, Learning By Questions, Dr Frost Maths, Heggarty Maths & Unifrog to name but a few!
We have taken the next step in our digital learning journey by providing pupils in Year 3 and above with a 1:1 electronic device.
In a 1:1 environment, the learning shifts from the traditional instructor-led model to become more pupil-centred.
Access to online learning tools gives the pupil options that naturally engage them and enable them to take ownership of how their learning goals are achieved. Pupils experience greater independence, greater task completion and a more efficient workflow with the ability to electronically manage and share tasks in a single environment.
Pupils benefit greatly from 1:1 in the development of their collaboration skills.
1:1 devices support the communication and joint reasoning that’s essential to team collaboration. By sharing a digital workspace, pupils create and edit content together, refine each other’s contributions and share information and ideas. Teachers help pupils engage in expressive activities by allowing them to choose their communication tools and encouraging pupils to work together to ‘show what they know’.
1:1 technology makes it possible for pupils to receive differentiated content and assignments, using a variety of methods and tools.
For example, our use of One-Note allows for content to be delivered within the class which is appropriate for the ability level of the individual child. Real time progress is monitored, and immediate feedback can be given. For pupils who require more of an academic stretch, more challenging work is provided, and this is particularly useful when assessments are being completed.
Pupils receive feedback in a myriad of ways. Teachers can digitally annotate a piece of work, leave voice recordings, a video, or a link to additional support online.
The ability to leave voice marking creates a more personal, formative conversation in which the pupil can respond in a similar way. This shows teachers that their feedback is being acted upon which is critical for student progress.
Meoncross School

pageCache.pageTitle: Pastoral Care - Student Support, Welfare & Wellbeing
pageCache.text:
Holistic Approach & Wellbeing
Prioritising the wellbeing of all our pupils
At Meoncross, we put as much emphasis on the wellbeing of our pupils, as we do their academic achievement. We know children will not achieve their best academically unless they are happy; therefore we put significant effort into ensuring all our pupils are well cared for, emotionally, and academically. This emotional resilience will allow pupils to be positively engaged and focused in lessons, as well as create enthusiasm around the pursuit of other opportunities that Meoncross has to offer.
All-round pastoral support
At Meoncross, we believe our dedicated and nurturing approach to pastoral care truly sets us apart. Our holistic ethos ensures that pupils not only achieve their full academic potential, but also grow into well-rounded, capable, and compassionate individuals, who are ready to thrive at college and beyond, and to contribute positively to the wider world. To support this, our Upper School benefits from the leadership of an Assistant Head (Pastoral), a long-serving, highly respected, and experienced member of staff who knows our pupils well and is always available to support them when challenges arise. This vital role is further strengthened by our two Pastoral Leads for Key Stages 3 and 4, alongside our committed team of Community Tutors. These staff members provide day-to-day pastoral care, building strong, supportive relationships with their tutees through daily interactions that promote wellbeing, engagement, and personal development.
Meoncross School

pageCache.pageTitle: Private School Admissions & Application - Apply For School
pageCache.text:
Admissions Process
Joining us is straightforward
Apply for a place at our exceptional school and put your child on the path to a fantastic educational experience. We have designed our admissions process to be as easy as possible and we will happily guide you every step of the way.
Get in touch with our friendly Admissions Team to chat about your child, check availability, and learn more about what makes our school so special.
Come along to one of our regular Open Events to experience the vibrant life of Meoncross, see our pupils and teachers in action and discover how your child could truly thrive here Alternatively, personal tours with our Admissions Manager are available at a convenient time. Contact us to book your visit.
When you're ready to take the next step, simply complete the registration and pay the £150 registration fee (our Admissions Manager will send full details). Then our Admissions Process can begin.
Your child will be invited to join us for taster days to meet their classmates and teachers while we assess their capabilities and behaviour.
Once we have received a satisfactory school reference, and gathered feedback from staff on the outcome of their taster days, you will receive your offer of a place. Your child’s Meoncross adventure is about to begin.
Simply complete the admissions documentation with a deposit of £350 to secure your child’s place.
Meoncross School

Mid-Year Admissions
Accommodating all pupils
Here at Meoncross School, we are in the position to be able to welcome new students all year round, so if you are looking for your child to start their new school within an academic year, we warmly invite you to come and meet with our Admissions Team. Whatever the reason for a mid-year start, we are here to help as much as we can, and we are very used to and experienced with welcoming children mid-year.
A smooth transition
Our experienced academic and pastoral teams will work together to ensure that the transition is as smooth as possible, with our main aim being that you and your child/ children feel to be a part of the Meoncross School community as soon as possible. One of the ways that we ensure this is with our carefully considered buddy system that begins straight away on our taster days.
Arrange a visit
We have many ways in which you can visit the school, whether that is a personal tour with our Admissions Team to see the pupils during everyday lesson time, or one of regular school in action open mornings where you are guided around by two of our pupils. The perfect chance to hear first-hand what life here is like from their perspective. Our Head and members of the SLT are also available to talk to. You can find out more about our upcoming events below, but please don’t hesitate to contact our Admissions Team to discuss a personal tour if you can't make any of these dates.
Something for everyone
Meoncross School prides itself on our nurturing pastoral care alongside academic excellence approach, which results in a thriving community for all. There are many opportunities to grow through our scholarships and ambassador roles, as well as our diverse co-curricular programmes, covering a wide selection of topics.
To arrange a time that is most convenient for you, please get in touch with our Admissions Department at 01329 666 017 or e-mail admissions@meoncross.co.uk where our warm and friendly team are ready to guide you through the process or have an informal chat.
We look forward to welcoming you into the Meoncross family.
Meoncross School

pageCache.pageTitle: School Transport & Private School Bus - Meoncross School
pageCache.text:
Transport To School
Pick up and drop off
All pupils are welcome onsite from 8.30am and should be in their classrooms/designated meeting area by the times listed below. We have a minibus service running across 4 key routes for your convenience. For the safety of our pupils, there is no parent parking in the car park. We operate a ‘drive-through-and-drop-off’ system in the mornings, and for collection and at the end of the day, there is parking along Burnt House Lane, or a car park at the village end of Burnt House Lane. These measures are in place to ensure the safety of our pupils, parents and staff, and we thank you for your cooperation.
Reception Class
Infants (Years 1-2)
Juniors (Years 3-6)
Upper School (Years 7-11)
Home to school transport
Early Years and Infants (Years 1-2)
Arrival: 8.30am Please arrive at 8.30am via Gate A if on foot, (or at Gate B if being dropped off by car). Parents are welcome to come into the school at the start of the school day. Please take your child to the astro pitch at the front of the school where they will be met by their year group teachers. Children will line up in form groups at 8.45am. Departure: 3.45pm Please wait by the coloured railings near the pirate ship where your child’s Form Teacher will bring your child to meet you.
Juniors (Years 3-6)
Arrival: 8.30am Please arrive at 8.30am via Gate A (or at Gate B if being dropped off by car). Parents are welcome to come into the school at the start of the school day and take your child to the Junior Playground where they will be met by their year group teachers. Children will line up in form groups at 8.45am. Departure: 3.45pm Please wait in the Junior playground where your child’s Form Teacher will bring your child to meet you at the end of the day. Year 6 - Please wait outside the Year 6 classrooms where your child’s Form Teacher will bring your child to meet you at the end of the day.
Upper School (Years 7-11)
Arrival: 8.30am Pupils should enter the school site independently and head to their form tutor room for Registration. Departure: 3.50pm Pupils are dismissed in class and may exit the school site independently.
Home to School transport
We currently operate a number of unchaperoned bus routes to and from school on a daily basis. Our Lee on Solent and Gosport route is operated with a Meoncross School minibus and driver, whilst Whiteley, Warsash and East Meon & Fareham, are serviced by our transport providers 'Beeline' and 'Jet Connect' respectively. Buses are timed to arrive in time for morning registration at 8.45am. Each afternoon pupils line up outside in the allocated area for their bus at 3.50pm and are checked onto the bus by a member of office staff and the bus driver, and depart the school at 4pm.
Lee on Solent & Gosport
Each stage of the journey has a different cost ranging from £3.29 - £5.75. Bookings for the bus can be requested for either every morning (5 trips), every afternoon (5 trips) or mornings and afternoons every day (10 trips). Bookings are for the whole term and paid for in advance. There will be no refunds for journeys not taken and there are no ad-hoc bus bookings.
Meoncross School
